access_links.label: DARTS: Evolving Resilience of the Global Food System to Production and Trade Shocks (JASSS 27(2) 1)
Companion article in PLOS Complex Systems

dedupe_keys.name: darts agent based model of the global food system for studying resilience to shocks

description: DARTS is an agent-based model of stylised food systems in which agents produce, earn income, trade and consume a single commodity food such as rice, used to study how the structure of a food system shapes its resilience to shocks. Each monthly step lets agents harvest if it is their region's harvest month, earn off-farm income, buy and sell food locally or internationally and consume it; shocks can temporarily cut production, remove local or international trade, or wipe out savings, and the model measures food satisfaction, the share of each agent's food requirement met, straight after the shock and over the following year, for groups such as the urban and rural poor. The provider is Hubert Fonteijn and co-authors at Wageningen, who describe it in the Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation (27(2) 1) and a companion PLOS Complex Systems article. Coverage is stylised worlds, not real countries. Version 1.0.0 of the NetLogo 6.2.0 code is available for download from the CoMSES Computational Model Library under CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0, published November 2023 and not peer reviewed there; the no-derivatives terms limit adapting it. Caveats: one food type, fixed requirements and synthetic geography. Simulation uses: comparing food system architectures under production or trade disruption and testing which agent groups lose food security first. Related records: PyTradeShifts (model-pytradeshifts) models real country trade networks.
